title: There’s No Excuse For a Dirty, Disorganized Home
author: M.A. Franklin
summary: M.A. Franklin of Foundation Father argues that a messy home is a spiritual and leadership problem before it is an organizational one, and he addresses both husband and wife. He rejects the idea that spotlessness is the goal, pointing to Proverbs 14:4 to say that a home used for raising children will be messy and that the mess must be managed, not ignored. His practical prescription is to put children to work on real chores, treating them as an asset that needs up-front investment, and to run a short weekly husband-led conversation over a shared chore list. He describes a spreadsheet and script tool he built with AI to email the list each week, but insists the conversation, not the tool, is the point. The deeper claim is that cleanliness only lasts when the household has a mission beyond rest and entertainment, such as weekly hospitality, so that chores become service to neighbor. The husband is charged with instilling that mission and winning buy-in.
points: A tidy home is not the goal in itself; the aim is joyful stewardship, and a house in use will be messy in ways that must be managed instead of ignored.
Children can be taught and supervised to do real household work, and the up-front investment pays off because they are an asset to the family.
A simple weekly chore list works only when husband and wife discuss time and capacity honestly, so the conversation matters more than the software.
Cleanliness sustained only for convenience will not last, so a household mission such as regular hospitality gives chores a purpose beyond themselves.
The husband is responsible for casting that mission and getting buy-in, which lets him encourage the family toward a higher calling instead of repeating that chores build character.
quotes: No amount of organization or help can root out bitterness. Even if you hired a maid, that person would not be able to clean the inside of a soul. It evinces a deeper spiritual problem.
First, some basic expectations. Spotlessness is not necessarily the goal. A perfect house, ready for a photoshoot, is not the goal. Joyful, righteous living is the goal.
Rather, the home should be well-enough kept that the family, at the drop of a hat, can spend about 30 minutes and be prepared to invite guests inside the door without being embarrassed.
Children are an asset. As such, they require some up-front investment. If you invest properly, they can be more valuable than you can possibly imagine.
The conversation is the point, and the husband needs to lead it, with input from his wife. Usually this doesn’t need to take longer than 15 minutes. Then put the list on the refrigerator.

Your household needs a mission beyond rest and entertainment. Something bigger than yourself, something you would not be able to accomplish alone. It can be as simple as radical hospitality, where you commit to having people over at least once per week or more.
Now, chores become part of something larger. Every sweep of the broom is in service to loving your neighbor. Every scrub of the toilet means something beyond the smell of bleach.
